gloss: to reflect on; to reconsider; to feel remorse

definitions.gloss: to reflect on one's actions; to feel remorse; to reconsider
definitions.explanation: To look back on one's own behavior or mistakes and recognize what went wrong, often with a sense of regret and a commitment to do better.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}の{行動|こうどう}を{反省|はんせい}した。
{彼|かれ}は{全|まった}く{反省|はんせい}していない{様子|ようす}だった。
examples.english: He didn't seem to feel remorseful at all.

examples.japanese: {失敗|しっぱい}を{反省|はんせい}して、{次|つぎ}は{同|おな}じ{間違|まちが}いを{繰|く}り{返|かえ}さないようにしたい。
examples.english: I want to reflect on my failure and make sure I don't repeat the same mistake next time.

notes:
A culturally significant concept in Japan. {反省|はんせい} goes beyond simple reflection — it implies acknowledging mistakes, feeling genuine regret, and resolving to improve. It is frequently expected in social and professional contexts when someone has done something wrong.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {深|ふか}く{反省|はんせい}する: to deeply reflect/feel remorse
- {反省|はんせい}の{色|いろ}がない: to show no sign of remorse
- {反省|はんせい}{点|てん}: points for reflection/improvement
- {反省|はんせい}{会|かい}: review meeting, post-mortem
- {反省|はんせい}{文|ぶん}: written apology/reflection

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japanese schools and workplaces, {反省|はんせい} is a routine practice. Students may be asked to write {反省|はんせい}{文|ぶん} (reflection essays) after misbehavior, and teams hold {反省|はんせい}{会|かい} (review sessions) after events or projects.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {後悔|こうかい}する: to regret — focuses on the feeling of wishing one hadn't done something, without the constructive element
- {振|ふ}り{返|かえ}る: to look back — neutral reflection without the implication of having done something wrong
